guidance.project.title: Get this project started
guidance.project.summary: A short guide to what belongs where and what to fill in first.
guidance.project.intro: The IDE separates project maturity, future work, and the record of what happened.
guidance.project.steps: Describe the project, its need, and the intended outcome here.
Use stages to move the project from v.0.0 to v.1.0; they provide an estimate when neither a manual value nor a measurable roadmap exists.
Put future actions in the backlog, context in the journal, and choices in decisions.
Use JSON export for backup and Markdown export for reading or sharing.
guidance.project.ideaCapture: The “New idea” button opens a classification tool for an idea that appears during a project. It does not replace this guide or create a separate project.
guidance.stage.title: Guide for {{version}}
guidance.stage.summary: Why this stage exists, which questions to ask, and how to know it is complete.
guidance.stage.fields: How to fill in the fields
guidance.fields.goal.label: Goal
guidance.fields.goal.description: The precise outcome sought during this stage.
guidance.fields.notes.label: Notes
guidance.fields.notes.description: Useful facts, ideas, constraints, and reasoning.
guidance.fields.deliverable.label: Expected deliverable
guidance.fields.deliverable.description: The observable evidence produced: a document, decision, prototype, result, or completed action.
guidance.fields.definitionOfDone.label: Done when
guidance.fields.definitionOfDone.descrip: Verifiable exit criteria, rather than a general feeling that the stage is finished.
guidance.stage.v0_0.why: Clarify the real need before jumping too quickly to a solution.
guidance.stage.v0_0.questions: What problem, need, or intention started this project?
Who is affected and in what context?
What concrete change would show that the project is useful?
guidance.stage.v0_0.example: Reduce the time spent each week manually gathering information from several places.
guidance.stage.v0_1.why: Understand the context, existing options, and unknowns before choosing a direction.
guidance.stage.v0_1.questions: What already exists and what can be reused?
Which people, sources, or experiences can clarify the need?
guidance.stage.v0_1.example: Compare three existing approaches and interview two people who currently perform the task.
guidance.stage.v0_2.why: Define a useful outcome and an initial scope small enough to move forward.
guidance.stage.v0_2.questions: What is the smallest genuinely useful outcome?
What is included, excluded, or postponed?
Which needs and constraints have priority?
guidance.stage.v0_2.example: The first version handles one type of case without automating exceptions.
guidance.stage.v0_3.why: Choose an approach and prepare the work before assembling its parts.
guidance.stage.v0_3.questions: Which steps, resources, and skills are needed?
Which dependencies or decisions must be resolved first?
Which risks deserve a preventive measure?
guidance.stage.v0_3.example: Create a four-part plan, identify responsibilities, and prepare a fallback option.
guidance.stage.v0_4.why: Assemble the essential parts into a first coherent whole.
guidance.stage.v0_4.questions: Do the main parts work together?
Which complete path can already be followed?
What is missing for a first testable version?
guidance.stage.v0_4.example: Combine the form, procedure, and tracking table into a complete but still imperfect workflow.
guidance.stage.v0_5.why: Produce a first usable version that can test the important assumptions.
guidance.stage.v0_5.questions: Who can safely try this first version?
Which observations or measures should be collected?
guidance.stage.v0_5.example: Ask two people to try the whole workflow and record blockers without polishing everything yet.
guidance.stage.v0_6.why: Correct the defects that prevent reliable use of the prototype.
guidance.stage.v0_6.questions: Which problems genuinely block or degrade use?
Which defects are reproducible and have priority?
How will a correction be checked for regressions?
guidance.stage.v0_6.example: Fix the three observed blockers and replay the test scenario after each change.
guidance.stage.v0_7.why: Try the solution in more realistic conditions with a still-limited audience.
guidance.stage.v0_7.questions: Who takes part in the beta and with which instructions?
Which feedback, incidents, and results should be tracked?
Which risks still justify limited access?
guidance.stage.v0_7.example: Open the solution to a small team for two weeks and collect all feedback in one place.
guidance.stage.v0_8.why: Stabilize the project using real feedback and prepare its finalization.
guidance.stage.v0_8.questions: Which feedback must be addressed before release?
Which improvements can wait for a later version?
Do the documentation and procedures reflect reality?
guidance.stage.v0_8.example: Address confirmed defects, postpone secondary requests, and update the guide.
guidance.stage.v0_9.why: Verify that the result is ready to be delivered, published, or adopted.
guidance.stage.v0_9.questions: Are the success criteria and obligations satisfied?
Has the final result been approved by the right people?
Are rollout, communication, and rollback prepared?
guidance.stage.v0_9.example: Run final acceptance, obtain approval, and prepare the launch checklist.
guidance.stage.v1_0.why: Deliver a usable result and organize continuity after launch.
guidance.stage.v1_0.questions: Is the result accessible to the people concerned?
Who will handle follow-up, maintenance, or evaluation?
How will incidents and future improvements be recorded?
guidance.stage.v1_0.example: Publish the approved result, hand over the guide, and schedule an initial evaluation.
